quotes.text: We’ve replaced some of our older APIs and no longer update their documentation.
We’ll communicate more information about this end of support through email.
We’ve also deprecated support for card payments in the Sources API, but don’t currently plan to turn it off.
Although unsupported, these APIs aren’t going away.

Old raw lines 8-25; new raw lines 9-26. The matrix groups the current family against Charges/Tokens/Sources for breadth of payment methods, SCA readiness, Terminal and future development; old raw lines 27-34, new raw lines 28-35.

Neither capture supplies migration setup, permission to start a legacy integration, an end date, API/SDK minima, client/server call examples or outcomes. The scoped transition and Charges companion guides distinguish a legacy stateful Source/Charge and browser Token from PaymentMethod instrument, PaymentIntent payment lifecycle, SetupIntent setup without charge and the separate Charge attempt. Old transition lines 26-46, November transition lines 27-53, November Charges lines 27-53, and detailed card migration lines 15-37. In the November Charges card example, Stripe.js tokenizes card details in the browser. The merchant sends that Token to its server, which creates the Charge. Separately, both dated transition guides allow legacy Source creation on the front end or server. Tokenization and Source creation are preparatory steps. Charge creation is separate, and fulfillment depends on verified payment success. In the newer Intent path, the server creates the Intent and handles status verification itself or via server webhooks, while the client can handle authentication with the client secret. See April transition lines 26-46, November transition lines 27-49 and November Charges lines 27-41. A refund request also remains distinct from a successful refund.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/older-apis, old raw lines 8-25 and 27-34 and new raw lines 9-26 and 28-35 establish the same guidance. Stripe no longer updates documentation for some replaced APIs and recommends Payment Intents, Setup Intents and Payment Methods for new features and migration. Both captures require migration for local payment methods using Sources, identify shutdown as a plan and point to later email information, and describe Sources card support as deprecated without a current shutoff plan on this route. They put Charges and old ACH under unsupported APIs still usable until an existing integration upgrades. The matrix groups the modern APIs as broader in payment methods and supporting SCA readiness, Terminal and future development, while the Charges, Tokens and Sources group lists cards and ACH and lacks those capabilities. The overview contains no account prerequisites, API minimum or runtime evidence. A PaymentIntent tracks a payment, SetupIntent saves for future use without charging, PaymentMethod represents an instrument and Charge records a specific attempt, according to the linked implementation context. In the November Charges card example, Stripe.js tokenizes card details in the browser. The merchant sends that Token to its server, which creates the Charge. Separately, both dated transition guides allow legacy Source creation on the front end or server. Tokenization and Source creation are preparatory steps. Charge creation is separate, and fulfillment depends on verified payment success. In the newer Intent path, the server creates the Intent and handles status verification itself or via server webhooks, while the client can handle authentication with the client secret. See April transition lines 26-46, November transition lines 27-49 and November Charges lines 27-41. source-stripe-legacy-apis.md already distinguishes November Charges card-payment creation from Charge reads and refunds, but its April-only older-APIs attribution omits the November repetition, its Sources card status lacks reciprocal context from the November Sources transition, and legacy ACH continued use needs the dedicated no-new-users qualification.

Keep the older ACH continued-use claim paired with the November ACH guide’s new-onboarding block. The grouped Older APIs matrix lists Cards/ACH for Charges, Tokens and Sources (old raw lines 27-34 and new raw lines 28-35). The separate April 20 Charges comparison says legacy Charges supported cards and all methods on the Sources API (raw/stripe-charges-vs-payment-intents-2025.md lines 24-29). Neither overrides the November Charges creation bar or the November Sources migration and new-integration restrictions. The November card-oriented transition, raw/stripe-payments-payment-methods-transitioning-2026-11-07.md lines 39-49, describes incomplete authorization and server retrieval or server webhook verification without restating a 48-hour timeout.
